title: Star Talent record and the Mardi Gras number
summary: The interviewer sorts out the Star Talent releases; Longhair says carnival numbers were being asked for at the time.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Okay, we're going to try to get to the records specifically and then, you know, tax your memories as much as you can. Let me... Yeah, so the Star Talent record, I think it was for you, you were right about the Mardi Gras in New Orleans, but that was never issued on Star Talent. No. Just the Ain't Got No Hair and the... Had to Call Bounce. Had to Call Bounce. No, no, it's Hey Now, Baby, Hey... No, it wasn't... What was the name of it? Wait, I got it right here. Bye Bye Baby. She Ain't Got No Hair and Bye Bye Baby was the first record. And then they also cut the Mardi Gras and the Had to Call but they never released it. So, where'd you get the idea for the Mardi Gras?
They didn't release it, it must have stopped them.
Yeah, yeah, I think they were going to, but I think they just recorded it. So, what, you told me one time that Mardi Gras in New Orleans was, you got an idea from somebody about that?
No, they were just asking for carnival numbers. You know, at that time they wanted a good carnival number. They had numbers about Christmas, they had New Year's, and most of all the holidays.
